title: GPS maps enter an endless render loop
trigger: Open Dashboard or GPS Map while at least one valid GPS point exists.
evidence: The shared map repeatedly sets a new center tuple from a freshly filtered array. The latest browser check recorded 91 copies of “Maximum update depth exceeded”. Dashboard and GPS Map both use this component.
fix: Memoize the filtered GPS data and skip center updates when coordinates have not changed.
repair: GPS filtering is memoized; coordinate-equivalent center updates are skipped. Both map views pass the render-loop regression.

title: One driver can depart on two vehicles at once
trigger: Approve two adjacent trips today for the same driver on different vehicles. Check both out before either returns.
evidence: Both departure requests returned HTTP 200. Both tickets became in_progress. Departure claims the vehicle but does not claim the driver or check another active outing.
fix: Atomically claim both vehicle and driver at departure, reject active outings and inactive drivers, and release the driver at arrival.
repair: Active outings claim their driver under a consistent row lock. A second departure with that driver returns a conflict.

title: A vehicle is released while another repair is open
trigger: Create and note two repairs for one vehicle. Complete the first repair while the second is still assigned.
evidence: The vehicle became available while the second repair remained assigned_mechanic. The vehicle can become bookable and leave the gate before all workshop work is finished.
fix: Release the vehicle only when no other assigned or ongoing repair holds it, with the check and update protected by the same vehicle lock.
repair: Completing one repair retains the vehicle maintenance hold while another repair remains active.

title: Concurrent requests bypass reservation overlap checks
trigger: Send simultaneous bookings for the same vehicle, driver and time window.
evidence: Five of six simultaneous requests returned HTTP 201 and created overlapping tickets; only one returned 409. The availability check runs before the create transaction and does not reserve the resources.
fix: Validate and create under vehicle/driver locks or a serializable transaction with conflict retry. Add a meaningful concurrency regression test.
repair: Booking creates and edits lock their driver and vehicle before availability checks. Concurrent overlapping requests accept exactly one booking.

title: Cancelling the final date erases approved fuel history
trigger: Fully approve a single-date ticket, then cancel its final scheduled date.
evidence: The approved fuel decision appeared in history before cancellation and disappeared afterwards. The allocation was changed from approved to cancelled. Whole-ticket cancellation already preserves settled decisions.
fix: Apply the existing pending-only cancellation predicate to per-date cancellation. Keep approved and declined decisions in the historical record.
repair: Canceling trip dates preserves approved and disapproved fuel decisions and their history.

title: Changing a user to Driver does not create a driver identity
trigger: Change an existing requester user to the driver role, then sign in again.
evidence: The new login reported the driver role, but its own driver list contained zero rows. The create-user path creates or links Driver; the update-user path only changes UserRole.
fix: Reuse driver identity linking/creation when assigning the driver role, in the same transaction as the role change.
repair: Assigning the driver role creates or reuses one linked Driver in the same transaction.

title: Scheduled preventive work leaves mileage and service history stale
trigger: Complete a scheduled service at 52,000 km for a vehicle recorded at 40,000 km.
evidence: The scheduled task completed, but Vehicle.mileage remained 40,000 and the service-history list contained zero rows. Predictive maintenance reads the vehicle odometer and canonical service history, so that completion cannot refresh its baseline.
fix: Write completed preventive work into canonical service history, validate the reading and advance the odometer. Define how task-level completions map to a service event.
repair: Preventive task completion advances mileage and writes canonical service history atomically; backwards mileage is rejected.

title: Blank optional dates prevent ordinary driver edits
trigger: Edit a driver whose birth date, license expiry or hire date is unset.
evidence: The form turns missing dates into empty strings and forwards them unchanged. A corresponding edit returned HTTP 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. This blocks name, status and photo edits for otherwise valid sparse driver records.
fix: Omit empty optional dates when creating records and define a nullable clear convention for edits. Normalize the form adapter to that contract.
repair: Blank optional driver dates are omitted from sparse edits. Explicit date clearing persists null through JSON and multipart updates.

title: A comma inside a participant name prevents booking
trigger: Enter one participant named “Dela Cruz, Juan”.
evidence: The form counts one person, then joins and splits names using commas. The submitted payload contains two names with participantsCount 1; the API returned HTTP 400 PARTICIPANTS_MISMATCH.
fix: Keep participant names as an array from individual form inputs through submission.
repair: Participant names remain arrays through booking and pending edits, preserving names containing commas.

title: Drivers receive Tool actions that cannot succeed
trigger: Sign in as a driver, choose Add Tool, complete the form and confirm submission.
evidence: The driver can open the form, but submission returned HTTP 403. Tool detail also exposes Edit while API POST/PATCH remain admin-only.
fix: Restrict the Add/Edit controls and creation route to administrators. Keep the permitted driver read experience.
repair: Tool Add/Edit controls and the creation route are restricted to administrators. Drivers retain permitted read access.

title: Changing a driver contact email hides their trips
trigger: Change the linked driver record’s email without changing the user login email.
evidence: The update returned HTTP 200 and retained the correct userId link. The driver dashboard then displayed “We couldn’t find a driver record for your account. Ask an admin to link it.” It matches email instead of the stable user identity.
fix: Preserve userId in the frontend adapter and identify the driver by that relationship.
repair: The driver dashboard uses the stable userId relationship, so changing contact email preserves account linkage.

title: Operational queues silently lose records after 100
trigger: Add 101 newer terminal tickets behind an older ticket awaiting fuel approval.
evidence: The actionable ticket was present before the fixture and absent from the first page afterwards, although its detail still showed pending_fuel_allocation_approval. The list returned 100 of 121 tickets. EVP, guard, driver and requester screens filter a fixed first page without pagination.
fix: Fetch status-filtered operational queues with pagination, or exhaust the appropriate pages. Add visible pagination to histories.
repair: Operational views fetch complete queues beyond the first 100 records. Requester history has visible page controls.

title: The pending trip edit form cannot be opened
trigger: Attempt to correct a pending booking in the normal ticket interface.
evidence: isEditing starts false and every setter sets it false. No Edit trigger exists, although a full edit form and owner/admin PATCH endpoint exist.
fix: Expose an Edit action for permitted owners/admins while the ticket is pending_admin_approval.
repair: Owners and administrators can edit pending tickets. Unchanged dates and outing IDs are preserved; changed local schedules retain the intended Manila time.

title: Frontend route permissions miss child and trailing-slash URLs
trigger: Sign in as a requester and visit /maintenance/ or /maintenance/add-maintenance directly.
evidence: Both maintenance interfaces rendered, including the creation form. The guard looks up the raw pathname; index routes use normalized keys and child/detail routes lack inherited allowedRoles. API write guards remain effective.
fix: Use the router’s matched route records and inherited role metadata instead of a raw pathname lookup. Align page actions with the resulting permission.
repair: Matched route metadata and resource-index policies guard child and trailing-slash routes while preserving valid role-specific detail links.

title: Missing detail records remain on a loading screen
trigger: Open a nonexistent tool, part, vehicle or trip detail.
evidence: The nonexistent tool screen rendered “Loading...”. The detail components return Loading whenever data is absent, including permanent 404/403/network errors, without an error or not-found branch.
fix: Distinguish initial loading from failed queries and missing records. Show a clear error/not-found state with retry or return navigation.
repair: Trip, tool, part and vehicle details show clear missing/error states with retry or return actions.

title: Maintenance calendar selection does not fill the date
trigger: Click a calendar day to create maintenance.
evidence: The calendar passes a date query parameter, but the add form never reads it and leaves the date blank. The user must repeat a choice they already made.
fix: Read and validate the route search parameter, then initialize the date field from the selected calendar day.
repair: Maintenance creation retains the selected calendar day, including week/day timestamp values, and rejects invalid dates.
